samples.summary: Split at offset 0 leaves the heading memory on the emptied half — the split-side mirror of `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` was never applied to `applySplitBlock`
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:220 `const after = cloneBlock(block)` / :256-258 `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel`) keeps `headingLevel` on `before` unconditionally, and `before` is the ORIGINAL block id. Enter at the very start of a *non-empty* bulleted heading takes the non-empty branch of `Doc.splitBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:303-340 — text length > 0, so `newType = 'list-item'`) and calls `store.splitBlock(blockId, 0, newId, 'list-item')`. `before` (= b1) ends up with empty inlines but still `headingLevel: 2`; `after` (= the block that now carries the heading TEXT) has it deleted. Consequence: un-listing the text bullet gives a paragraph (the Heading 2 is unrecoverable), while the empty leading bullet un-lists into an empty Heading 2. The same asymmetry lands in the CRDT: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2132-2143 builds the after node without `headingLevel` and never touches the before node's attribute. The new merge predicate (`block is a list item, has a remembered level, has no text of its own`) is exactly the condition that is true of `before` here, but nothing calls it on the split path — the design note at docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177 only reasons about the *after* half.

samples.summary: Yorkie `mergeBlock` decides the tree-side `headingLevel` removal from the cached block, in the one method that documents cache/tree divergence
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2189 computes `mergeDropsHeadingMemory(firstBlock)` from the cached block, then removes the attribute from the tree at :2200. Twelve lines later the same method warns: "Read inline count from the actual tree, not the cache, because previous split/merge operations can leave the tree with a different number of inline nodes than the cache (e.g. split fragments)" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2202-2205). If the cache and tree disagree about whether the first block holds text, the predicate and the CRDT write disagree with each other and with `applyMergeBlocks`' cache-side delete, leaving `headingLevel` present in the tree but absent in the cache (or vice versa) until the next reload. The tree-derived inline data is already available in this method and could drive the predicate.

verdict.reason: Every quoted location checks out. applySplitBlock (block-helpers.ts:219-220, 256-258) deletes headingLevel only from the `after` half and leaves it on `before`, which retains the original block id. Doc.splitBlock (document.ts:303-307, 330-331, 340) routes a NON-empty bulleted heading with offset 0 into the split path with newType='list-item', and text-editor.ts:2100-2104 reaches it with pos.offset unfiltered (no offset-0 guard, unlike editor.ts:3257/3276). The result is exactly as described: `before` = empty list-item still carrying headingLevel, `after` = the block that now holds the heading text with headingLevel deleted; yorkie-doc-store.ts:2132-2143 reproduces the same asymmetry in the tree and never clears the before node's attribute. The newly introduced predicate mergeDropsHeadingMemory (block-helpers.ts:279-285) is literally true of `before`, yet its only callers are the merge/paste paths (block-helpers.ts:293, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2187, text-editor.ts:3582) — nothing on the split path. The design note (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177) and the task non-goal (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:53-57) reason only about the after half receiving body text, and the single split test (test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:212-227) splits at end-of-text, so the offset-0 mirror is neither guarded nor deliberately sanctioned. Consequence is user-visible: the heading level becomes unrecoverable for the text that was the heading (and a subsequent Backspace merge then strips it via the new predicate), which is a violated-invariant/unconsidered-consumer issue at major under this lens.

finding.summary: Paste reaches the same 'heading memory travels onto text that was never a heading' defect the new merge guard closes, without passing through it
finding.evidence: The delta establishes the provenance rule that a `list-item`'s remembered `headingLevel` must not survive when foreign text is folded into the block (`mergeDropsHeadingMemory`, block-helpers.ts:279). The paste path bypasses it: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3575-3580 appends the pasted inlines to the existing head block and then unconditionally sets `headBlock.type = firstPasted.type` and `headBlock.headingLevel = firstPasted.headingLevel`; the same happens for the tail block at lines 3604-3607. `copySelectedBlocks` copies the memory verbatim for a partial slice (text-editor.ts:3404: `if (block.headingLevel !== undefined) cloned.headingLevel = block.headingLevel;`), so pasting a bulleted heading into a paragraph makes the paragraph a `list-item` carrying a heading level, and the block's own pre-existing body text is then promoted to a Heading N on un-listing — exactly the #783 follow-up symptom. Confirming needs a paste round-trip test; the write path is unguarded either way. Fix could live either at these two assignments or by routing them through the same helper.

verdict.reason: The alleged bypass does not exist in this repository. The finding says paste "unconditionally sets headBlock.headingLevel = firstPasted.headingLevel" and likewise for the tail block. In the working tree, both sites route through the guard helper: text-editor.ts:3606 `headBlock.headingLevel = pastedHeadingLevel(firstPasted, headOwnTextLen)` and text-editor.ts:3636 `tailBlock.headingLevel = pastedHeadingLevel(lastPasted, tailOwnTextLen)`. `pastedHeadingLevel` (text-editor.ts:42-45) returns undefined when the pasted block is a `list-item` and the destination contributes text of its own — exactly the provenance rule `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:279-285) enforces on the merge path. The single-block paste path calls `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` directly (text-editor.ts:3582, 3585), with the helper imported at text-editor.ts:4. So the scenario "pasting a bulleted heading into a paragraph makes the paragraph a list-item carrying a heading level" is blocked whenever the destination has its own text; when the destination is empty the memory legitimately carries the whole block, consistent with the merge rule. The finding's cited line ranges do not match the file contents, and the fix it proposes ("routing them through the same helper") is already implemented. Copying `headingLevel` verbatim in `copySelectedBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3426) is real but is not a bypass, since the paste-side helper decides survival.
